learningObjectives.title: Sikh beliefs about God and the Gurus
The Guru Granth Sahib and the Gurdwara

questions.q: Which phrase opens the Mool Mantar and expresses the core Sikh belief that there is only one God?
questions.explain: Ik Onkar means 'There is one God' and begins the Mool Mantar, the foundational statement of Sikh belief.

questions.q: Who was the first Sikh Guru and the founder of Sikhism?
questions.explain: Guru Nanak (1469-1539) was the first Guru and founder of the Sikh faith.

questions.q: Who was the tenth and last human Guru of Sikhism?
questions.explain: Guru Gobind Singh was the tenth human Guru and passed Guruship to the Guru Granth Sahib.

questions.q: Sikhs describe God as 'nirankar'. What does this teach about God?
options: God is one of many gods
questions.explain: Nirankar means 'without form', teaching that God cannot be limited to a physical shape or image.

questions.q: Which term best describes Sikh belief about God?
questions.explain: Sikhism is monotheistic, teaching belief in one single God (Waheguru).

questions.q: A Sikh sits quietly each morning repeating 'Waheguru' to focus the mind on God. Which practice is this?
questions.explain: Nam Japna is meditating on and repeating God's name to remember and focus on the divine.

questions.q: What is the holy scripture of Sikhism?
questions.explain: The Guru Granth Sahib is the central holy scripture and is regarded as the living Guru.

questions.q: Which Guru compiled the Adi Granth, the first version of the Sikh scripture, in 1604?
questions.explain: Guru Arjan, the fifth Guru, compiled the Adi Granth in 1604 and installed it in the Golden Temple.

questions.q: In which script is the Guru Granth Sahib written?
questions.explain: The Guru Granth Sahib is written in Gurmukhi, the script standardised by Guru Angad.

questions.q: Why do Sikhs regard the Guru Granth Sahib as the final, eternal Guru?
options: Guru Gobind Singh declared it the everlasting Guru, ending the line of human Gurus
It was written directly by God
It is simply the oldest Sikh book
Only priests are allowed to read it
questions.explain: Before his death, Guru Gobind Singh gave permanent Guruship to the scripture, making it the eternal living Guru.

questions.q: In the gurdwara, on what raised throne is the Guru Granth Sahib placed to show its authority?
questions.explain: The Guru Granth Sahib rests on a raised throne (takht) beneath a canopy, showing it is treated as a living Guru.

questions.q: A visitor to a gurdwara covers their head and removes their shoes before entering the prayer hall. This shows respect chiefly for what?
questions.explain: Covering the head and removing shoes shows respect for the Guru Granth Sahib, honoured as the living Guru.

questions.q: The langar (free communal kitchen and meal) most clearly demonstrates which Sikh value?
questions.explain: Everyone sits and eats together in the langar regardless of status, expressing the Sikh belief in equality.

questions.q: In which year did Guru Gobind Singh found the Khalsa?
questions.explain: The Khalsa was founded at Vaisakhi in 1699 by Guru Gobind Singh.

questions.q: What name is given to the first five Sikhs initiated into the Khalsa?
questions.explain: The Panj Pyare, or 'five beloved ones', were the first members of the Khalsa.

questions.q: Which festival commemorates the founding of the Khalsa?
questions.explain: Vaisakhi (Baisakhi) in April celebrates the founding of the Khalsa in 1699.

questions.q: What does the Kara, one of the Five Ks, symbolise?
options: That God is eternal, with no beginning or end
That a Sikh must fast regularly
That Sikhs must remain silent in worship
questions.explain: The Kara is a steel bracelet whose unbroken circle symbolises that God is eternal and unending.

questions.q: Which of the Five Ks refers to uncut hair, showing acceptance of God's creation?
questions.explain: Kesh is uncut hair, kept as a sign of respect for God's natural creation.

questions.q: A Sikh volunteers each week to cook and clean in the gurdwara without pay. Which Sikh duty is being carried out?
questions.explain: Sewa is selfless, voluntary service given to others and to the community without reward.

questions.q: A Sikh man is initiated into the Khalsa through the Amrit ceremony. Which name is he expected to take?
questions.explain: Male members of the Khalsa take the name Singh ('lion'), while women take Kaur ('princess').
